description: A scientist in the arctic needs to get enough vitamin D and vitamin C in his diet by drinking orange and apple juice. Each box of orange juice contains 10 units of vitamin D and 8 units of vitamin C. Each box of apple juice contains 12 units of vitamin D and 6 units of vitamin C. Since the scientist prefers apple juice, he must drink at least 3 times as many apple juice boxes and orange juice boxes. However, he must also drink at least 3 orange juice boxes. To avoid a vitamin C overdose, the scientist can consume at most 300 units of vitamin C. How many of each juice box should he drink to maximize his total vitamin D intake?

VitaminDOrange.definition: Amount of vitamin D in each box of orange juice

VitaminCOrange.definition: Amount of vitamin C in each box of orange juice

VitaminDApple.definition: Amount of vitamin D in each box of apple juice

VitaminCApple.definition: Amount of vitamin C in each box of apple juice

PreferenceRatio.definition: Minimum ratio of apple juice boxes to orange juice boxes

MinimumOrangeBoxes.definition: Minimum number of orange juice boxes to be consumed

MaxVitaminC.definition: Maximum allowed units of vitamin C intake

objective.description: "Maximize the total vitamin D intake from consuming orange and apple juice boxes"

constraints.description: The number of apple juice boxes consumed must be at least 3 times the number of orange juice boxes consumed
The number of orange juice boxes consumed must be at least 3
The total vitamin C intake from orange and apple juice must not exceed 300 units

AppleBoxes.definition: Number of apple juice boxes consumed

OrangeBoxes.definition: Number of orange juice boxes consumed
